items.title: A Lebesgue number for a family of neighborhoods
items.gist: For a compact subset of a pseudometric space and a family of sets one of which is a neighborhood of each point of that subset, there is a positive radius such that every ball of that radius around a point of the subset lies in a single member of the family.
items.departures: The members of the family are not assumed to be open; each is only required to be a neighborhood of the points it has to cover.

items.title: Subdivision points of an interval
items.gist: For a nonnegative step size d, define the nth subdivision point of [a,b] by t_n = min{b, a + nd}.
items.departures: The text uses the minimum formula as the definition of the underlying interval point. The linked Lean lemma proves that Mathlib's clipped-step construction has this value for a nonnegative step size.

items.title: The values of a concatenation of paths
items.gist: A concatenation of two paths takes, at a parameter in the first or in the second half of the unit interval, a value of the first or of the second path at a rescaled parameter.

parts.gist: At a parameter whose value is at most one half, the concatenation agrees with the first path at any parameter whose value is twice as large.
At a parameter whose value is at least one half, the concatenation agrees with the second path at any parameter whose value is twice as large, less one.

items.departures: The rescaled parameter is given as a point of the unit interval together with the equation its value satisfies, rather than computed from the original parameter.

items.title: A subpath of a path confined to a set
items.gist: If a path sends every parameter of a closed interval into a set, then the subpath between any two parameters of that interval takes all of its values in the set.

items.title: Subdividing a path along a family of sets
items.gist: If every parameter has a neighborhood that the path sends into some member of a family of sets, then the path can be cut at finitely many increasing parameters running from zero to one so that each consecutive subpath has its range inside a single member.

items.title: Covers generate the fundamental groupoid
items.gist: If every point of the space has some member of a family of subsets as a neighborhood, then the images of the functors induced by the inclusions of the members generate the whole fundamental groupoid as a subgroupoid.
items.departures: The members of the family are not assumed to be open and no connectedness is assumed of them or of their intersections; each member is only required to be a neighborhood of the points it covers.

items.title: Gluing functors out of fundamental groupoids
items.gist: Functors to a fixed category out of the fundamental groupoids of the members of such a family, agreeing after restriction to every pairwise intersection, glue to a single functor out of the fundamental groupoid of the whole space.
items.departures: The target is an arbitrary category, the members of the family are not assumed to be open, and neither they nor their intersections are assumed connected.

items.title: Gluing two functors out of fundamental groupoids
items.gist: When the interiors of two subsets cover the space, two functors out of the fundamental groupoids of those subsets which agree after restriction to the fundamental groupoid of their intersection glue to a functor out of the fundamental groupoid of the space.
items.departures: The two subsets need not be open: only their interiors have to cover the space, and no connectedness is assumed.

items.title: Covers generate the fundamental group
items.gist: If every point of the space has some member of a family of subsets as a neighborhood, every member contains the basepoint, and every intersection of two members is path connected, then the images of the fundamental groups of the members generate the fundamental group of the space.
items.departures: The members of the family are not assumed to be open, and path-connectedness is assumed of every intersection of two members, which for a member paired with itself is the member itself.

items.title: The homomorphism out of the fundamental group of the space
items.gist: Homomorphisms to a monoid out of the fundamental groups of two subsets, whose interiors cover the space and which are path connected along with their intersection, and which agree after restriction to the fundamental group of the intersection, induce a homomorphism out of the fundamental group of the space.
items.departures: The target is only assumed to be a monoid, and the two subsets need not be open: only their interiors have to cover the space.

items.title: Uniqueness of the induced homomorphism
items.gist: Two homomorphisms to a monoid out of the fundamental group of the space are equal as soon as they agree after restriction along the inclusions of both subsets.
items.departures: The target is only assumed to be a monoid, and the two subsets need not be open: only their interiors have to cover the space.

items.title: The based Seifert--van Kampen theorem
items.gist: If the interiors of two subsets cover the space, the two subsets and their intersection are path connected, and all three contain the basepoint, then the square of fundamental groups formed by the four homomorphisms induced by the inclusions is a pushout in the category of groups.
items.departures: The two subsets need not be open: only their interiors have to cover the space. The basepoint of the intersection is the basepoint of the space, which lies in the intersection because it lies in both subsets.
